criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.fiveMeans: No claim contradicts or goes beyond the sources; every number matches the sources.

anchors.excerpt: Source: 'Online orders rose from 20k to 40k.' Document: 'Online orders tripled to 60k, making online the largest channel.'
anchors.why: The number is wrong and the 'largest channel' claim is not in the source.

anchors.excerpt: Source: 'Online orders rose from 20k to 40k; retail held at 42k.' Document: 'Online orders doubled to 40k, closing in on retail at 42k.'
anchors.why: Every figure matches and the comparison follows directly from the source.

criteria.name: Coverage
criteria.fiveMeans: Every must-convey fact is conveyed, clearly enough that a reader would come away knowing it.

anchors.excerpt: Must convey: 'MFA is required for admin accounts', 'access reviews run quarterly', 'orphaned accounts are disabled within 24 hours'. Document mentions only MFA.
anchors.why: Two of three required facts are missing.

anchors.excerpt: Document: 'Admins must use MFA. Every quarter, managers re-approve who has access, and accounts left behind by departed staff are switched off within a day.'
anchors.why: All three facts are conveyed, in plain terms.

criteria.name: Calibration
criteria.fiveMeans: Explains what a non-expert reader would not know and does not re-explain the obvious.

anchors.excerpt: 'A company sells products to customers. Revenue is money. The CAC was $120 and LTV:CAC hit 3.1x.'
anchors.why: Belabors trivia while leaving CAC and LTV:CAC unexplained.

anchors.excerpt: 'It cost $120 in marketing to win each new customer (CAC), and each customer is expected to bring in about three times that over their life, a ratio investors treat as healthy.'
anchors.why: Explains the unfamiliar ideas once, briefly, and skips the obvious.

criteria.name: Explanatory structure
criteria.fiveMeans: Leads with the point, builds logically, and headings are informative.

anchors.excerpt: Headings: 'Slide 1', 'Slide 2', 'Other'. The conclusion (the pilot should be extended) appears only in the last paragraph.
anchors.why: Mirrors the source order, uninformative headings, buries the point.

anchors.excerpt: Headings: 'The pilot cut errors by half', 'Why the night shift gained most', 'What extending it would cost'. The first paragraph states the recommendation.
anchors.why: Leads with the point; each heading tells the reader what the section shows.

criteria.name: Visual explanation
criteria.fiveMeans: Charts, diagrams or annotated figures carry real information and match the data (WSJ-grade).

anchors.excerpt: [Chart: 'Growth' | categories A, B | values 1, 2] next to a paragraph about quarterly churn.
anchors.why: The chart is decorative, unlabeled and unrelated to the text's data.

anchors.excerpt: [Chart: 'Online orders doubled in a year' | Widget orders by channel, thousands | Retail 40 to 42, Wholesale 30 to 28, Online 20 to 40 | highlight: Online, up 100%]
anchors.why: Title states the finding, units given, values match the source, the key change is highlighted.

criteria.name: Glossary quality
criteria.fiveMeans: Glossary terms are the ones the original audience assumed; explanations are short and correct.

anchors.excerpt: Glossary: 'Company: an organization.' 'Quarter: three months.' (SIEM and EDR, used throughout, are not defined.)
anchors.why: Defines the obvious and misses the real jargon.

anchors.excerpt: Glossary: 'SIEM: a system that collects security logs from many tools in one place so analysts can search and alert on them.' 'EDR: software on each laptop or server that records suspicious activity and can isolate the machine.'
anchors.why: Picks the assumed terms; each definition is one short, correct sentence.

criteria.name: References
criteria.fiveMeans: Every used and every skipped source is listed correctly, with a reason for each skipped one.

anchors.excerpt: References: 'campaign-review.md'. (The job also used funnel.csv, and a login-walled URL was skipped; neither is listed.)
anchors.why: A used source and the skipped source are missing.
All used sources listed, and the skipped one appears with its reason.
